At Genmab, we are dedicated to building extra[not]ordinary® futures, together, by developing antibody products and groundbreaking, knock-your-socks-off KYSO antibody medicines® that change lives and the future of cancer treatment and serious diseases. We strive to create, champion and maintain a global workplace where individuals’ unique contributions are valued and drive innovative solutions to meet the needs of our patients, care partners, families and employees.

Our people are compassionate, candid, and purposeful, and our business is innovative and rooted in science. We believe that being proudly authentic and determined to be our best is essential to fulfilling our purpose. Yes, our work is incredibly serious and impactful, but we have big ambitions, bring a ton of care to pursuing them, and have a lot of fun while doing so.

Does this inspire you and feel like a fit? Then we would love to have you join us!

**About The Role

**Genmab is seeking a Project Manager CMC Product Lifecycle Management to

• join the CMC Life Cycle Management (LCM) Team and support our growing portfolio of commercial products globally.

The LCM team is responsible for managing the CMC lifecycle activities of Genmab’s commercial products and manufacturing oversight, ensuring supply continuity, regulatory compliance, and successful execution of post-approval activities throughout the product lifecycle. In this role, you’ll work closely with LCM Product Lead and colleagues across Commercial Supply Chain, MSAT, Regulatory CMC, Commercial QA and External Manufacturing to ensure seamless execution of lifecycle management activities.

The CMC Life Cycle Management Team is part of CMC Project & Portfolio Management (PPM) which also includes the Early-Stage Development, Late-stage Development and External Manufacturing teams. CMC Project & Portfolio Management resides within CMC Development and Manufacturing, based in Denmark.

This role offers a unique opportunity to contribute to the continued growth of Genmab's commercial portfolio while working in a highly collaborative and cross-functional environment at the interface of development, manufacturing, supply, and regulatory affairs.

**Responsibilities

**

• Work alongside the LCM Lead to provide manufacturing oversight and execute lifecycle activities for an assigned manufacturing track (DS, BI, CI or DP) after commercial launch, supporting batch release and reliable supply. The LCM Lead retains overall product accountability.

• Lead operational governance with internal functions and partners/CMOs, aligning priorities, preparing decisions, tracking progress and actions, and providing input on CMO performance.

• Collaborate with internal and external stakeholders on daily operations to ensure manufacturing oversight (ie. Deviation management, change control, complaint handling, etc) , support batch release and supply, issues resolution/escalation and quality/regulatory compliance.

• Coordinate technical issue resolution and manage track risks with relevant experts, ensuring required assessments, documentation and mitigation actions, and escalating issues with proposed next steps.

• Drive manufacturing changes, projects and improvements within agreed scope, timelines and budgets.

• Support implementation of CMC commitments and Post-approval change management related to assigned product manufacturing track (i.e DS, BI, CI, DP) and support coordination of submission documentation preparation across stakeholders and CMOs/Partners.

• Support initiatives to optimize yield, reduce cost of goods, and enhance robustness of manufacturing and testing processes

• Help establish and improve LCM processes, governance, tools and ways of working, incorporating lessons learned.

**Requirements

**

• Master's degree in science or related technical discipline (e.g. engineering, biotech, pharmaceutical, biochemistry, biology) or equivalent experience;

• 4+ years of experience in biopharmaceutical industry, preferably within manufacturing operations, lifecycle, product management for commercial products.

• Experience in building relations and influencing multi-functional teams within multicultural organizations.

• Proven track record in CMC project management, manufacturing operations management or product management across development and commercialization activities.

• Experience managing and defining project coordination activities and tasks in a structured, regulated environment.

• Prior experience with commercial product lifecycle management and oversight of Contract Manufacturing Organizations (CMOs) is considered an advantage.

• Broad understanding of global cGMP requirements and regulatory expectations across major markets

• Excellent communication and stakeholder management skills, with fluency in English

• Demonstrated ability to work effectively in cross-functional and multicultural environments

• Strong organizational skills with the ability to manage multiple priorities, balance competing demands, and deliver against project timelines

• Team player with the ability to collaborate with diverse stakeholders.

• Result- and goal-oriented, committed to contributing to Genmab’s success

The proposed gross annual/hourly base salary range for this position, in the primary location, based on a full time schedule is:

DKK597.312,00---895.968,00

The final salary offer will depend on several factors, including your skills, qualifications, and experience.

In addition to base salary, this position is eligible for additional forms of compensation, such as discretionary bonuses and long-term incentives.

**Benefits

**When you join Genmab, you become a part of a culture that supports your physical, financial, social, and emotional well-being. Our benefits include, but are not limited to:

• Pension

• Health insurance and wellness benefits

• Paid time off

• Employee support programs

Further details on eligibility for compensation and benefits based on the role will be provided during the recruitment process.

**About Genmab

**Genmab is an international biotechnology company with a core purpose to improve the lives of patients through innovative and differentiated antibody therapeutics. For 25 years, its hard-working, innovative and collaborative team has invented next-generation antibody technology platforms and harnessed translational, quantitative and data sciences, resulting in a proprietary pipeline including bispecific T-cell engagers, antibody-drug conjugates, next-generation immune checkpoint modulators and effector function-enhanced antibodies. By 2030, Genmab’s vision is to transform the lives of people with cancer and other serious diseases with Knock-Your-Socks-Off (KYSO®) antibody medicines.

Established in 1999, Genmab is headquartered in Copenhagen, Denmark with international presence across North America, Europe and Asia Pacific. For more information, please visit Genmab.com and follow us on LinkedIn and X.

Genmab is committed to protecting your personal data and privacy. Please see our privacy policy for handling your data in connection with your application on our website Job Applicant Privacy Notice (genmab.com).

**The Impact You'll Make

**As our Communication Coordinator, you’ll help bring our Digital and Lifecycle Services portfolio to life for colleagues, partners, customers, and end users around the world.

You’ll join the Digital & Lifecycle Services Communications team and contribute to strengthening the visibility of our service business through engaging visual communication, content, marketing materials, and events. Working across an international organization, you’ll have the opportunity to turn complex topics into clear and compelling communication.

This fixed-term role is available for one year and offers the opportunity to build hands-on experience across graphic design, communication, and service product launches in a global environment while contributing to solutions that support energy efficiency throughout the product lifecycle.

**What You’ll Be Doing

**

• Work together with the Communication Manager to support daily internal and external communication activities, build content for thought leadership topics, and help with creation of focus business marketing narratives.

• Create engaging visual communication, including icons, visual concepts, posters, images, and other branded materials using Adobe tools.

• Develop content supporting marketing and communication activities across Digital & Lifecycle Services.

• Collaborate with global marketing teams to create and launch marketing materials such as sales presentations, fact sheets, product descriptions, and other communication assets.

• Contribute to our Service Partner Program, developing branded materials such as presentations, guides, fact sheets, visuals, and other supporting content.

**What We're Looking For

**We’re looking for someone who combines creativity with a structured approach and enjoys turning ideas into communication that is easy to understand and visually engaging.

**To Be Successful In This Role, You Bring

**

• Experience with graphic design, content creation, communication, or marketing and familiarity with design tools such as Adobe Photoshop, Adobe InDesign, video editing skillset, or similar.

• A structured, hands-on approach and the ability to coordinate tasks and projects involving different stakeholders

• Strong communication skills and the ability to work effectively in a matrix organization with international and cross-functional environment.

• Professional fluency in English, both written and spoken.

• Relevant education in communication, marketing, business, design, or a related field.

Experience with B2B marketing, business consultancy, campaigns, agency work, or service-related businesses would be an advantage, but it is not essential. Most importantly, you are curious, collaborative, and motivated to create communication that makes an impact.

**What You'll Get From Us

**You'll help engineer a better future by contributing to solutions that make a real difference around the world.

In this role, you’ll gain broad experience across visual communication, content creation, global marketing collaboration, and events, while working with colleagues and stakeholders across an international organization.

We'll support your career growth with mentoring, learning opportunities, and access to global career paths.

You'll have the flexibility, autonomy, and support you need to do your best work while maintaining a healthy work-life balance.

You'll be part of an inclusive workplace where people of all backgrounds are respected, valued, and empowered to succeed.

You'll receive a competitive rewards package that includes benefits such as an annual bonus, paid vacation, pension plans, health insurance, and more. As a global company, these benefits vary by country and contract.

**Ready to Make a Difference?

**If you’re excited about combining creativity, communication, and collaboration to help make complex solutions clear and engaging, we’d love to hear from you.

You don’t need to meet every preferred qualification to apply. If this opportunity interests you and you believe your experience and perspective could add value to the team, we encourage you to apply.

**Our Commitment to Transparency

**Salary ranges listed reflect only primary location and currency. For local salary ranges and specific benefits in your preferred hiring location, please ask your Talent Acquisition representative for more information.

The actual salary offer will carefully consider a wide range of factors, including your skills, qualifications, experience, and location. Any benefits listed do not promise or guarantee any particular benefit or specific action. They may depend on country or contract specifics and are subject to change at any time without prior notice.

Want to know more? Please visit our **FAQ Page.

**All qualified applicants will receive consideration for employment without regard to race, color, religion, sex, sexual orientation, gender identity, national origin, age, disability, veteran status, or other protected category.

**Help hospitals deploy, operate and get the most from UNEEG software solutions

**_At UNEEG Medical, we are on a clear mission: improve epilepsy care and enhance patients' quality of life through objective, real-world EEG data. UNEEG EpiSight Solution, our sub-cutaneous EEG monitoring solution enables remote monitoring of brain activity in people with uncontrolled epilepsy and is already making an impact across Europe and the US. We combine the agility of a small company with the high standards of the medical device industry.

_**Your role and team:

**We are looking for an Application/IT Supporter who will be responsible for the technical deployment, support and ongoing operation of UNEEG's software solutions. You will help onboard new hospital customers, with a primary focus on the US market, while ensuring excellent service and operational continuity for our existing customers.

You will initially be part of Technology and later join the new Customer Enablement & Governance team. Working closely with the Project Lead, Customer Enablement & Governance, you will be the technical bridge between hospital IT teams and colleagues across Commercial, Clinical Operations and Technology. The role includes both remote and on-site support, and travel can be expected.

**Your main responsibilities will be:

**

• Plan, install, configure and test data transfer infrastructure solutions in hospitals

• Provide remote and on-site support for installations, upgrades, operation and troubleshooting

• Train hospital IT staff and system administrators to maintain deployed solutions effectively

• Monitor and maintain hospital servers, cloud clients and Microsoft Azure environments

• Troubleshoot networking, data communication, application and system performance issues

• Configure and manage virtual machines, containers and Kubernetes environments, and deploy patches and updates

• Document support cases and technical issues in Jira and collaborate with software developers on resolution and product improvements

• Maintain deployment procedures, troubleshooting guides and other technical documentation in line with healthcare IT and data security requirements

**You will thrive in this role if you:

**

• Are service-minded, outgoing and persistent, and enjoy working directly with customers

• Take ownership, follow up rigorously and solve problems before they arise

• Can manage several tasks at the same time while staying structured and attentive to detail

• Communicate clearly with both technical and non-technical stakeholders

• Enjoy collaborating across commercial, clinical and software development teams

• Are flexible when customer needs occasionally require support across time zones or outside normal working hours

**Your background:

**

• An education as an IT Support Technician or Data Technician, ideally focused on infrastructure, or a relevant degree in software development, infrastructure or a related field

• Experience or strong interest in customer-facing technical service or IT support; newly educated candidates with the right mindset are also encouraged to apply

• Proficiency in Microsoft Azure, virtualization and container-based environments, including Kubernetes

• Knowledge of relational databases, such as SQL Server, and scripting

• Ability to troubleshoot networking, application and system performance issues

• Experience with defect tracking and monitoring tools, such as Jira, Prometheus, Grafana or Azure Monitor

• Fluent professional English, both written and spoken

**It will be an advantage if you have experience with:

**

• Healthcare IT, hospital environments or deployment in public-sector organizations

• Healthcare data standards, hospital IT security protocols or clinical trial workflows

• ITIL or similar service management methodologies

• Data protection and privacy requirements, including GDPR and HIPAA

• Supporting international customers in Europe or the US

• Relevant certifications, such as Microsoft Azure Administrator or Kubernetes Administrator

Applicants must be eligible to work in Denmark and possess a valid work and residence permit if applicable. At this time, we are unable to support work permit applications or sponsorships.

**What we offer:

**

• A key role in supporting secure and scalable customer solutions in a growing medical device company

• Close collaboration with skilled colleagues and international hospital stakeholders

• A workplace with great energy, social activities and a culture of togetherness

• A role based at our modern HQ in Allerød with good facilities and easy access

At UNEEG, your ideas matter, your work makes a difference, and your colleagues have your back.

**Who to contact:

**For more details about the job, please contact Senior Director, Technology, Kim Heegaard Hansen at +45 25 65 75 01.

**How to apply:

**Apply through our Careers site.

All applications must be in English and are treated confidentially. We screen applications and invite candidates for interviews on an ongoing basis.

**About UNEEG Medical

**UNEEG Medical pioneers ultra long-term subcutaneous EEG monitoring to help physicians optimize treatment for epilepsy patients. Our UNEEG EpiSight solution provides objective insights into seizure burden, enabling more personalized care. We collaborate with leading institutions across Europe and the US to help patients regain control of their life. At UNEEG Medical, we are currently 40 dedicated people with diverse backgrounds. Our HQ is in Allerød with subsidiaries in the UK, Germany, Austria and the US. Our core values Togetherness, Integrity, and Dedication guide our work as we catalyze brain health therapy with real-world data.

_Do you want to join a global leader in renewable energy infrastructure investments? If so, come and join Copenhagen Energy Islands (CEI), a Copenhagen Infrastructure Partners (CIP) subsidiary company exclusively dedicated to developing energy hubs globally. We are currently looking for a Director to join our team.

_**Team

**Energy hubs will be the next generation of energy infrastructure assets. They will be critical in enabling cost-efficient deployment of large-scale renewable energy to achieve energy security and to reach ambitious global decarbonization targets, while maintaining cost competitiveness of the energy system. Energy islands, or energy hubs, are multifunctional energy infrastructure projects, involving large-scale renewable energy production integrated with conversion technologies to deliver electrons and molecules to demand centers. Copenhagen Energy Islands (CEI) is a company dedicated to originating and developing these projects.

You will be working closely together with an experienced team in a high paced, dynamic environment. We bring experts together with backgrounds in commercial, regulatory, development, legal, consulting and financial careers, to name a few.

We are a strong, social, and multi-national team with a passion for making a difference. Our collective character can be described as creative, dedicated, resourceful and humble. We are excited to work on something that is complex and will enable a step-change for the renewable industry.

**Role

**As a Director you will supervise several teams that work on opportunities in a number of markets. You will oversee the activities in technical, commercial, stakeholder and financial workstreams; and you will drive our external relationships with partners, advisors, and (non-)governmental organizations.

Your responsibilities will be to:

• Maximize the CEI investment value of the energy hub opportunities you work on

• Coordinate development activities with workstream managers that form part of the project development team

• Build and mature the investment cases for the CEI project you work on

• Own the project financial model and ensure that the model is maintained and used consistently across the projects

• Be the CEI focal point for our (joint venture) partners

• Manage the processes related to joint ventures, fund raising, divestitures; including negotiation of agreements and transaction documents

• Develop insights and high-quality presentations for internal and external stakeholders

• Advise CEI leadership team regarding general corporate matters such as portfolio management and resource allocation considerations

• Support CEI fundraise activities, including managing certain workstreams

• Play an active role in origination of new project opportunities and develop in-depth understanding of target markets

• You will help to manage, train and develop the Managers, Associates and Analysts, and will contribute to the positive, professional and collegiate working environment

• Participate in our activities to grow the team, such as interviewing and ranking candidates.

**You

**The work environment at CEI is lean, stimulating and demanding, within a global context. We are therefore looking for a self-starting, collaborative, and high-performance professional with an entrepreneurial drive. You have 15+ years of relevant experience from project development or infrastructure investment organizations.

Moreover, you have a background in offshore wind, hydrogen, Oil & Gas or other energy development and track record in bringing complex investments successfully to Final Investment Decision.

Key qualifications include:

• Knowledge of regulatory environment in the energy sector, and familiar with stakeholder engagement practices to shape desired outcomes

• Corporate Development and M&A knowledge

• Experience in commercial negotiations

• Ability to contribute to the overarching logic of business case when dealing with senior leadership and to step into the detail when discussing project specific aspects

• Experience in rapidly growing teams and businesses as well as exposure to critical governance structures and processes in an international environment is preferable

• Team player with the confidence to exercise judgement appropriately, engaging with colleagues at all levels of seniority

• Advanced communication skills with fluency in written and spoken English

• Ability to work well under pressure and take on responsibility

• You are proactive, think ahead and stay hands-on.

It is the expectation that frequent presence in Copenhagen is necessary for success.

**The process

**Please apply online as soon as possible as applications will be processed on an ongoing basis. For questions related to the role, please reach out to our Talent Acquisition team at recruitment@cipfs.com. We do not include CV's and Cover Letters sent by email.

As we continue to improve our candidate experience, diversity and avoid unconscious bias, please avoid having a photo in your CV. We commit to an inclusive recruitment process and equality for all applicants.

Please be aware that we will not accept speculative CV submissions for any of our roles from recruitment agencies, and any unsolicited candidate submissions will be exempt from any payment expectations and ownership.

**Building value that matters

**Founded in 2012, Copenhagen Infrastructure Partners P/S (CIP) is a global fund manager and leading investor in energy infrastructure. CIP builds value that matters by developing and constructing critical infrastructure projects that shape the future of energy.

Through its funds, CIP invests in power generation (solar and wind), energy storage, transmission and distribution, advanced bioenergy, low-carbon fuels and carbon capture.

With 15 funds currently under management, CIP is trusted by over 200 of the world’s largest and most sophisticated institutions, having raised EUR ~43 billion to date.

CIP has projects in more than 30 countries, with presence on the ground through a network of +2,300 professionals with extensive experience and knowledge within the fields of renewable energy project development and regulated infrastructure. In addition, CIP has a broad range of competencies within corporate finance, mergers & acquisitions, engineering, construction, project development, and project management.

Headquartered in Copenhagen, CIP operates from key locations across the globe, including offices in Hamburg, Munich, London, Amsterdam, New York, Tokyo, Melbourne, Luxembourg, Kuala Lumpur, Seoul, and Singapore. In addition, CIP has 17 local project offices globally.

For more information, visit www.cip.com.

jobs.occupation: Manager of Automation & IT Project Management at Novo Nordisk Engineering
jobs.description:
Manager of Automation & IT Project Management at Novo Nordisk Engineering

If you’re energised by leading people and complex technical projects and you thrive in a changing, multidisciplinary environment, we’d love to hear from you!

Who we are

We are a leading pharma engineering company shaping the future of API pharma engineering globally. Leveraging the expertise of 2,000+ employees across Denmark, India, and the US, we design, build and optimise pharmaceutical manufacturing facilities that are essential to the health and well-being of patients everywhere.

Our success is driven by passion, innovation, and collaboration — with our customers and across our teams and disciplines. If you share our dedication to a noble cause and our passion for API pharma engineering, then NNE is the place for you.

About the role

We are looking for a Manager of AIT Project Management to join our AIT Project Management leadership team. As a team, we are working on some of the largest and most technically complex pharma projects in Denmark, using the latest technologies across Automation and IT.

Together with the AIT Project Management leadership team, you will lead and develop a department of 15 Project Managers delivering highly technical projects in a GMP-regulated pharmaceutical environment. Your contribution will be important in ensuring high performance and employee wellbeing, while securing the right resources and competencies for our growing project portfolio.

You will work closely with Project Directors, customers, and Sales to support business development, follow up on new opportunities and ensure the right staffing across our projects. You will also contribute to creating a positive and engaging working environment across our wider team of more than 50 highly skilled Project Managers.

Our Project Managers bring experience across Process Automation, SCADA, PLC, IT/OT, PI, PAT, MES, and automated solutions. Project execution ranges from traditional PMP-based planning and execution to agile methodologies and the use of ADO, depending on the project area and customer requirements.

How you might spend your days

As a Manager of AIT Project Management, you’ll be:

• Leading, coaching, and developing a motivated team of Project Managers, ensuring high employee engagement and wellbeing

• Ensuring the right resources and competence mix are in place to support our growth strategy and project pipeline

• Working closely with Project Directors, customers, and Sales to support project delivery, business development, and new opportunities

• Strengthening Project Management processes within AIT and driving continuous improvements

• Supporting project execution and, when needed, taking on smaller assignments as a Project Manager

Who you are

We care about who you are as a person. In the end, how you work, and your energy is what impacts the results we achieve as a team. As a person, you are:

• A supportive leader who listens, provides constructive feedback, and motivates others to succeed

• Committed to ongoing coaching and the wellbeing and development of your employees

• A team player who leads by example and collaborates effectively across different areas and levels

• A strong communicator with a positive, holistic, and analytical mindset

• Structured and effective in your work, with an open and engaging management style

What you bring to the role

In all positions, there are some things that are preferred, and others, a bonus. If you do not meet all the qualifications listed below, you are welcome to offer alternative experience that you think would be valuable in this role:

• You hold a bachelor's degree in engineering or a related technical discipline, or bring equivalent relevant experience

• You have at least four years of experience leading Project Managers and/or technical specialists

• You have a background as a Project Manager

• You have knowledge of the pharmaceutical industry

• You are fluent in written and spoken English and Danish

Life at NNE

NNE is short for Novo Nordisk Engineering. And for all of us who work here, NNE means so much more.

At NNE, you become part of a vibrant, project-based environment built on close day-to-day collaboration. The role is therefore primarily on-site, with physical presence at the workplace expected five days a week. Limited flexibility for occasional remote work may be accommodated in line with business needs.

We are, at our core, a people business and, as such, committed to continuously developing our people and the way we work together. We do not expect you to know it all from day one, and we truly believe a great start makes a real difference. We therefore welcome new colleagues with our award-nominated onboarding programme, supported by a range of in-house talent and development initiatives designed to support your long-term growth.

You can read more about the benefits we offer here.

Did we spark your curiosity? If you’re ready to join our passion, let’s hear from you.

Deadline of application is 15th November 2026

Questions before applying? Send us a quick text to arrange a convenient time to chat. Please contact VP of AIT Project Management Timme Traberg-Andersen +45 3079 9436.

Please note:

• We only accept applications submitted through our online recruitment system

• You do not need to attach a cover letter, but please include a few sentences about why you are applying in your resume or CV

• We invite to interviews on a running basis.

Fair hiring:

At NNE, we are committed to an inclusive recruitment process and equal opportunities for all job applicants. To maintain fairness, we request that you refrain from including a personal photo in your CV.

We have an exciting opportunity for a seasoned Logistics Procurement Category Manager to join the Group Procurement function at Royal Unibrew.

Are you a passionate procurement and supply chain professional with expertise in Logistics and a demonstrated track record of positively influencing across internal and external ecosystems to unlock end to end value and efficiencies to fuel sustainable growth?

As Group Category Manager – Logistics, you will report to the CPO and lead the development and execution of the Group Logistics procurement strategy across road freight including line-haul and last mile distribution, ocean freight, warehousing and related logistics services including pallets. You will combine strategic category leadership with hands-on execution, working closely with local market organisations,

The role will be based at our HQ in Faxe, Denmark.

**Main Responsibilities

**Strategy Development:

• Define and execute a multi-year procurement category strategy for Logistics that balances local execution with strategic priorities to support the group’s overarching goals.

• Leverage a strong external radar and category expertise to identify, evaluate and act on emerging opportunities and risks, i.e. external supplier landscape, commodities, industry best practices, digitalisation and automation and EU legislative environment.

**Category And Supplier Relationship Management

**

• Optimise category management processes, elevate sourcing and contract management processes, and build best practices with the market teams and stakeholders. Increase utilisation of eSourcing and development of digital tools to support cost modelling, benchmarking, and contract management.

• Develop supplier collaboration platforms with key suppliers across the group to unlock operational efficiencies, process enhancements, digital innovation, and to accelerate sustainability and circularity initiatives.

**Value Delivery, Efficiency And Business Partnering

**

• Deliver cost savings, supply chain efficiencies and carbon reduction targets. Establish ways of working with stakeholders to measure relevant KPIs, track initiatives, manage risk and deliver multiyear productivity plans.

• Ensure early engagement and alignment with relevant stakeholders on business strategy to maintain a fit for purpose and efficient logistics network driving optimal cost to serve to fuel sustainable business growth.

• Provide category leadership and inputs into on strategic projects, integration, and network optimisation.

• Streamline processes and drive digitalisation agenda.

**Ideal Candidate

**

• Bachelor’s degree. Professional CIPS qualification or similar will be considered.

• Min. 8 years of relevant procurement experience in logistics categories in an international or matrixed organisation. Nordics and CPG industry experience is a plus.

• Comprehensive knowledge of procurement processes, ERP systems, procurement tools and network modelling, including a strong data analytics skillset and commodity management experience.

• Excellent communication, gravitas and influencing skills to build relationships with senior stakeholders internally and externally.

• Team player with a service-oriented mindset but is also not afraid to challenge the status quo or be the critical friend when required.

• Project and change management - track record for initiating and embedding change.

• Ability to balance strategic thinking with hands on execution.

• Energised by challenges, white spaces, and complexity.

• Enthusiastic, solution-oriented approach.

• Passion for developing and coaching teams.

**What Success Looks Like

**Success in this role means creating a Logistics procurement organisation that is recognised as a strategic business partner, delivering measurable value beyond price reduction.

The successful candidate will establish strong Group category governance while enabling local ownership, build strategic supplier partnerships, increase data and digital maturity, strengthen resilience and sustainability, and continuously identify opportunities to improve the total cost, service and efficiency of Royal Unibrew's logistics network.

At Royal Unibrew, you'll find the industry's most dedicated, energetic, and experienced colleagues. Together, we build the best framework for a job that precisely matches your everyday life and career aspirations.

Royal Unibrew produces, markets, sells, and distributes quality beverages. We are a consortium of more than 35 breweries and beverage producers from across Denmark, known especially for our traditional, locally-rooted brands such as Faxe Kondi, Egekilde, Royal Beer, Ceres, and Odense Pilsner, as well as partner brands like Pepsi MAX and Heineken.

Today, we are the second-largest beverage company in Denmark. Our journey began in 1856, and we still maintain a strong commercial focus, a clear growth strategy, and an ambitious sustainability strategy - both domestically and internationally.

You'll have over 1500 colleagues in Denmark and more than 2700 colleagues outside the country, including in Finland, Italy, France, Norway, Canada, the Netherlands, and the Baltic countries.

With us, you'll be part of challenging the boundaries of sustainable production and distribution. You'll help ensure a diverse range of beverages that bring people together - on the dance floor, during the third half, or over a meal - all while contributing to strengthening Danish sports, music, and community life.

jobs.occupation: Project Manager, EndoIntelligence Solutions, Global R&D
jobs.description:
Are you an experienced Project Manager with a background in medical device development? Do you enjoy leading complex development projects and coordinating work across internal teams and external development partners? Then you may be the Project Manager we are looking for in EndoIntelligence Solutions within Global R&D.

In this role, you will lead a strategically important development project and work closely with a global and cross-functional team to ensure successful project execution from planning through delivery.

We believe the best ideas come from a mix of in-person collaboration and focused individual work. That's why this role is based in Augsburg or Ballerup and follows a hybrid working model, with three days per week in the office and two days working from home.

**Key Responsibilities

**As Project Manager, you will:

• Lead a cross-functional development project through all phases of the product development process.

• Drive project planning, execution, follow-up, and reporting of scope, timeline, budget, risks, and key decisions.

• Coordinate activities across engineering disciplines and key stakeholders.

• Manage and maintain strong collaboration with external development partners and suppliers.

• Facilitate project governance activities, including Steering Committee reviews and decision-making forums.

• Ensure project documentation and deliverables are completed in accordance with Ambu's quality system and applicable regulatory requirements.

• Create transparency, alignment, and engagement across the project team and stakeholder landscape.

• Support the continuous improvement of project management practices and lessons learned.

**Suggested candidate profile

****Skills

**Skills and experience can be gained in many ways, and we understand that the perfect candidate cannot be defined on paper. However, you are likely to succeed in this role if you:

• Hold a technical degree within engineering or a related field.

• Have experience leading the development of complex medical device hardware, including electronics, mechanics, embedded systems, and integration across disciplines.

• Have worked closely with external development partners and suppliers and understand how to manage outsourced development activities, technical deliverables, timelines, and risks.

• Have experience working with internal and external development teams across different regions, including Asian and European countries, and bring the cultural awareness needed to adapt ways of working and build effective collaboration across cultures.

• Are comfortable navigating a complex stakeholder environment and driving alignment across functions.

• Bring a structured and proactive approach to project execution and risk management.

• Have strong communication and leadership skills and enjoy working with international teams.

• Are fluent in written and spoken English.

**Ambu – a visionary and international workplace where your efforts matter

**At Ambu, you will become part of an international organization with ambitious growth plans and a strong innovation agenda. We work in cross-functional teams and value collaboration, transparency, and continuous improvement. You will have the opportunity to contribute to innovative healthcare solutions while developing your professional and personal capabilities in a dynamic environment.

Apply directly through our job portal. We review applications on an ongoing basis.

**THE OPPORTUNITY

**Ready to shape the marketing experience for one of the most exciting categories in Nordic e-commerce?

We are looking for a Marketing Manager for a maternity cover of approximately 13 months to drive the customer-facing journey and category performance across our Kids department. From everyday essentials to seasonal collections, footwear and accessories, you will bring the category to life through engaging campaigns, inspiring content and a seamless shopping experience across our channels.

This is your chance to join a passionate, fast-paced team where creativity meets commercial strategy, and where your work makes a real impact on how customers discover and shop Kids at Boozt.

**What You Will Do

**As our Marketing Manager for the kids category, you will play a key role in planning and executing marketing activities across onsite, CRM and campaign touchpoints, ensuring that the category stays relevant, engaging and commercially strong.

**Your Main Responsibilities Will Include

**

• 
Develop and execute quarterly and yearly Kids marketing plans, aligned with commercial priorities and seasonal initiatives.

•

jobs.description:
We are looking for a highly motivated and dynamic postdoc for a one-year position to commence 1 March 2027 or after agreement.

  Introduction

  Antimicrobial resistance is a growing global health challenge that highlights the need for innovative therapeutic strategies beyond conventional antibiotic treatment.

  Host-directed antimicrobial strategies are attracting increasing interest as complementary approaches to conventional antimicrobial therapy. Recent studies have demonstrated that a novel synthetic compound improves survival in methicillin-resistant Staphylococcus aureus (MRSA)-infected Caenorhabditis elegans. Furthermore, previous studies in mammalian cells suggest that the compound may exert immunomodulatory effects, raising the possibility that stimulation of host defence pathways contributes to protection against infection.

  This project aims to determine whether the novel synthetic compound can stimulate innate immunity and enhance host defence pathways in C. elegans and thereby contribute to protection against MRSA-infection. Using a combination of immunology, microbiology, and transcriptomics, the successful candidate will lead the experimental investigation of the phenotypic and transcriptional responses underlying this protective effect. All experimental work will be conducted in C. elegans.

  Required qualifications

   	
• A PhD in immunology, infection biology, microbiology, molecular biology, biomedical sciences, pharmacology, or a related discipline. 	
• Hands-on experience with the maintenance and experimental use of Caenorhabditis elegans, preferably as an infection model. 	
• Knowledge to innate immunity and host defence pathways. 	
• Demonstrated ability to conduct independent research. 	
• Excellent written and oral communication skills in English.   Highly desirable qualifications

   	
• Knowledge to innate immunity and host defence pathways in Caenorhabditis elegans. 	
• Experience with bacterial culture and experimental microbiology. 	
• Experience with omics-data analysis (such as RNA-seq data). 	
• Experience with quantitative PCR (qPCR) and gene expression analysis. 	
• Experience with RNA interference (RNAi) and gene-silencing approaches. 	
• Knowledge of antimicrobial compounds and antimicrobial resistance. 	
• Experience contributing to external funding applications. 	
• A strong publication record relative to career stage.   Key responsibilities

  The postdoctoral fellow will conduct research within host-directed antimicrobial strategies and innate immunity. The successful candidate is expected to contribute to student supervision, assist in the preparation of external funding applications, and lead the dissemination of research findings through scientific publications and presentations, as well as participate in other academic activities.

  Research environment and collaboration 

  The successful candidate will be based in a research environment with expertise in C. elegans biology and will interact closely with collaborators possessing complementary expertise in immunity, microbiology, and bioinformatics. The interdisciplinary nature of the project provides excellent opportunities for scientific exchange and the development of skills across multiple disciplines while independently driving the research project.

  Further information

  Further information on the Department is linked at https://ivh.ku.dk/. Inquiries about the position can be made to Associate Professor Tina V. A. Hansen, alstrup@sund.ku.dk

  Starting date and duration

  The position is available from 1 March 2027 or after agreement. The position is a fixed-term, full-time postdoctoral appointment for a period of one year.

  Terms of employment

  The position is covered by the Memorandum on Job Structure for Academic Staff.

  Terms of appointment and payment accord to the agreement between the Ministry of Finance and The Danish Confederation of Professional Associations on Academics in the State.

  You can read more about salary levels in the state sector www.loenoverblik.dk (in Danish).

  The application, in English, must be submitted electronically by clicking APPLY NOW below.

  Please include

• Diplomas (Master and PhD degree or equivalent) 	
• Research plan – description of current and future research plans 	
• Complete publication list 	
• Separate reprints of 3 particularly relevant papers 	
• Contact information for 2–3 references.   The deadline for applications is Tuesday 24 November 2026, 23:59pm CET

jobs.description:
The Department of Anthropology, School of Culture and Society, invites applications for a three-year position as assistant professor in relation to the research project “Stories from my new life: Mobile transitions and social becomings among resettled refugees in Denmark” (TRANSIT).

An assistant professorship is a full-time, three-year training position that involves research and teaching at the BA and MA level and includes an obligatory course in university teaching for assistant professors. The position will commence on 1 February, 2027 or as soon as possible thereafter. 

Place of employment: Department of Anthropology, Moesgaard Allé 20, 8270 Højbjerg, Denmark.

The Faculty of Arts is committed to creating an inclusive working environment and therefore encourages all qualified candidates to apply, regardless of personal background, gender, sexual orientation, age, disability, ethnicity etc.

The position
The position will be associated with the research project TRANSIT at the Department of Anthropology and is a combined teaching and research position.

Here is a brief description of the TRANSIT project:

In 2021-2024 app. 600 Congolese women and children were resettled in Denmark under the UNHCR resettlement program. TRANSIT is concerned with resettled refugees’ life transitions, understood as a set of complex legal, social and existential transitions that are particularly urgent in the context of resettlement: 1) the transition from youth to adulthood; 2) the transition from being single to being married; and 3) the transition into old age and, ultimately, death. The project aims to establish a collaboration between Aarhus University, VIVE – The Danish Center for Social Science Research, FLUGT – Refugee Museum of Denmark, DFUNK – Dansk Flygtningehjælp Ungdom and a large group of resettled families in order to: a) create a mobile pop-up exhibition to be presented across Denmark in 2029; b) develop research-based teaching materials for pupils in the final years of Folkeskolen and in Gymnasiet on what it means to be resettled and start a new life in Denmark; and c) publish articles in leading peer-reviewed journals – based on a range of qualitative and quantitative data – on storytelling and life transitions following resettlement.

The selected candidate is expected to do individual fieldwork, be main responsible for a work-package (developing research-based teaching material with FLUGT – Refugee Museum of Denmark), and to be a dedicated member of the project team and engaged in all the project activities and responsibilities.

The position is offered with a view to attracting qualified applicants with an established and well-documented research record in innovative and internationally recognized research within anthropology and a specialization in migration and refugee studies, collaborative methods and creative forms of research dissemination. 

Research
The selected applicant will be expected to contribute to core activities at the School of Culture and Society and Aarhus University in general and contribute to the Department of Anthropology’s research activities and output in particular. They will be expected to take an interest in interdisciplinary research collaboration within the Department of Anthropology, the School of Culture and Society, the Faculty of Arts, and beyond. 

The selected applicant will also be expected to develop new research projects with internal and external partners and to raise external research funding. The applicant’s research credentials and publication record within the field, e.g. anthropology, migration and refugee studies, collaborative methods and creative forms of research dissemination, will be assessed not just on existing publications and other research contributions but also on research potential.

Past research output will be assessed based on the active research time of the applicant in question. We therefore ask applicants to specify any career breaks they have had (for instance due to maternity/paternity leave or sick leave) so we may discount these periods when assessing research productivity.

Teaching
The position will involve some teaching (up to 33% of the time) as agreed upon with the Head of the Department and the project PI. The selected applicant will be required to teach and supervise at BA and MA levels of the department’s degree programs in Anthropology and Human Security and will be expected to have teaching experience at university level. 

We emphasise the importance of maintaining a professional and respectful relationship between staff and students, so applicants should be able to demonstrate and exemplify their commitment to participatory teaching initiatives and student involvement as part of their teaching portfolio.

Qualifications
Applicants must hold a PhD or equivalent qualifications in anthropology or a related discipline. They must also be able to document the following: 

• An internationally oriented research profile documented through relevant academic publications, and possibly other research contributions, at the international level
• Experience of university-level teaching and a commitment to teaching development and the supervision of student projects
• Experience of or interest in active participation in international research collaboration
• Experience of or interest in obtaining external research funding
• Experience of or interest in research dessimination for a non-academic audience
Applicants are asked to submit:

• A concise statement of motivation for applying for the position, including a description of experience with public research dessimination (maximum two pages).
• A full CV (one page).
• A full publication list (research outputs and public dissemination)
• A maximum of two publications.
Only submitted publications will be assessed; a list of publications is not sufficient. As a result, applications without submitted publications will not be assessed.

References or recommendations should not be included with the application. Applicants who are selected for a job interview may be asked to provide professional references.

Language and further information
Applicants can teach and supervise in English at university level.

If the selected applicant is not fluent in Danish, they will be expected to acquire the language within a period of approximately two years. 

To maintain and develop the department’s research environment, the person appointed is expected to be present at the department on a regular basis.

Applications must be uploaded in English.

For further information about the TRANSIT project (including the project description), please contact, PI, Professor Mikkel Rytter, mikkel.rytter@cas.au.dk

For further information about the application procedure, please contact Human Resources: iks-hr-sag@au.dk.

Knowledge exchange
It is expected that the selected applicant will engage in knowledge exchange as described in the strategy for the Faculty of Arts Strategy Arts 2020-2025 (au.dk), for instance research cooperation with private companies, government consultancy, cooperation with civil society partners or the public dissemination of knowledge. Applicants should document any prior experience within the field of knowledge exchange.

School of Culture and Society
The School of Culture and Society is a vibrant research community engaged in understanding the cultural and social conditions that shape human life. Our work examines how people interact with their environments, from prehistory to the present and across both local and global contexts. Through cross-sector and cross-disciplinary partnerships, we aim to support research innovation and contribute to addressing the major questions facing society. In both research and education, we are committed to bringing the humanities into active dialogue with partners beyond the university.

The School is committed to:

• Promoting an international environment characterized by active academic and interdisciplinary collaboration.
• Encouraging innovative and experimental approaches to research, teaching, and communication.
• Cultivating environments that generate new knowledge and educate students for the future.
• Advancing broad engagement with digital humanities.
• Upholding a deep commitment to addressing both local and global societal challenges.
• Creating an inclusive, diverse, and sustainable workplace and organization.
Read more about the school here School of Culture and Society - Aarhus University

International applicants
International applicants are encouraged to check Family and work-life balance in Denmark (au.dk) and Attractive working conditions (au.dk) for further information about the benefits of working at Aarhus University and in Denmark, including healthcare, paid holidays and, if relevant, maternity/paternity leave, childcare and schooling. Aarhus University offers a broad variety of services for international researchers and accompanying families, including a Relocation and onboarding services for international AU staff and career counselling for expat partners. For information about taxation, see Taxation aspects of international researchers’ employment by AU.

Qualification requirements
Applicants should hold a PhD or equivalent academic qualifications.

Formalities
• Faculty of Arts refers to the Ministerial Order on the Appointment of Academic Staff at Danish Universities (the Appointment Order).
• Further information on qualification requirements and job content may be found in the Memorandum on Job Structure for Academic Staff at Danish Universities.
• Further information on the application and supplementary materials may be found in Application Guidelines.
• The application must outline the applicant's motivation for applying for the position, attaching a curriculum vitae, a teaching portfolio, a complete list of published works, a research plan, copies of degree certificates and examples of academic production (mandatory, but no more than two examples). Please upload this material electronically along with your application. Please note that although the application process can be completed in the Aarhus University system without up-loading publications or a teaching portfolio, applications that do not include uploaded publications as well as a teaching portfolio (or equivalent documentation of teaching experience and qualifications) will not be considered.
If nothing else is noted, applications must be submitted in English. Application deadline is at 11.59 pm Danish time (same as Central European Time) on the deadline day.

Aarhus University’s ambition is to be an attractive and inspiring workplace for all and to foster a culture in which each individual has opportunities to thrive, achieve and develop. We view equality and diversity as assets, and we welcome all applicants.

Shortlists may be prepared with the candidates that have been selected for a detailed academic assessment. A committee set up by the head of school is responsible for selecting the most qualified candidates. See this link for further information about shortlisting at the Faculty of Arts:  shortlisting

Terms of employment
• Appointment shall be in accordance with the collective labour agreement between the Danish Ministry of Finance and the Danish Confederation of Professional Associations.
Salary and terms of employment are governed by the Cirkulære om overenskomst for akademikere i staten  (in Danish). You will be employed as Assistant Professorship at base pay level 4–8 with additional supplements in accordance with the Cirkulære om protokollat om visse ansættelsesvilkår for videnskabeligt personale ved universiteter (in Danish).

The job content and qualification requirements are described in further detail in the Ministerial Order on the Appointment of Academic Staff at Universities.

About Arts
The Faculty of Arts is one of Northern Europe’s most significant faculties for research and higher education in the humanities, theology and education. Within this broad academic scope, the faculty comprises approximately 700 researchers, 200 PhD students, 9,000 Bachelor’s and Master’s degree students, and 1,500 further and continuing education students. We believe that the best ideas arise when different perspectives meet – and that research, teaching and innovation are best developed in dialogue with the surrounding society.

You can find more information here: Faculty of Arts |  Aarhus University

jobs.occupation: 171626 Associate professor in Clinical Proteomics and Data-Driven Biomarker Discovery for Neurodegenerative Disease (Fixed-Term, 5 Years)
jobs.description:
Faculty of Health and Medical Sciences

  University of Copenhagen

   

  The University seeks to appoint an time limited associate professor at the Department of Drug Design and Pharmacology to commence March 1st 2025 or as soon as possible thereafter

  Department of Drug Design and Pharmacology is committed to advancing human health through discovery, design, and evaluation of safe and effective medical treatments. To achieve this, we work in a dynamic and committed academic community, that bridges health science and life science in a translational and innovative approach from molecule to patient. We value interdisciplinary research and education, development of individual competences, and finding solutions to todays and tomorrows challenges in society. The department furthermore prioritizes sustainability in all aspects of research and education.

  The department is organized in six research sections and furthermore houses Center for Pharmaceutical Data Science Education and Center for Protein Design. Further information on the Department can be found at: https://drug.ku.dk/

  Job description 

  We seek an established researcher to lead an independent research programme at the interface of clinical proteomics, molecular neuropathology, and translational neuroscience. The successful candidate will drive biofluid biomarker discovery and drug-target identification in Huntington’s disease and other neurodegenerative disorders, contributing to the department’s data-driven target and drug discovery activities and to its concerted effort to integrate data science and AI into research and teaching. Using state-of-the-art mass spectrometry-based proteomics, multi-omics, and machine learning, the candidate will connect mechanistic insight to clinical application through disease-relevant models and human sample cohorts, supporting AI-powered translational prediction and clinical decision support for personalized treatment.

  Responsibilities

  The associate professor’s responsibilities will primarily consist of:

   	
• Research, including publication/academic dissemination of results to the scientific community and attraction of external funding 	
• Develop, organize, and conduct research-based teaching, including associated examination. 	
• Research leadership, including guidance and supervision of students and researchers 	
• Obligation to share knowledge with the rest of society, including participation in public debate 	
• Academic assessments 	
• Engage in outreach and/or innovation activities both within the Department and towards academia, the clinic, and industry in general.   Qualifications of the applicant

  When evaluating applicants, primary emphasis will be placed on the applicant's ability to document original scientific work of the highest international standard, an innovative mindset, and strong ambitions for advancing teaching within the fields of biochemistry and pharmacology, with particular focus on teaching on compulsory courses at the BSc and MSc levels.

  Applicants already having sustainability integrated in all aspects of their research and teaching, or a clear plan for doing so, will have preference. Likewise, a clear and structured plan for internal and external collaborations will be given positive consideration.

  Overall criteria for the position: 

  To be qualified for an associate professor position, you will be assessed according to these five overall criteria for recognising merit at the University of Copenhagen: Research, teaching, innovation & societal impact, organisational contribution and leadership. Find information about each criterion.

  Furthermore, each applicant must be able to document:

   	
• Research qualifications at the level that can be achieved by satisfactorily completing a period of employment as an assistant professor/postdoc, but may also be obtained in other ways 	
• Teaching qualifications and pedagogical competencies 	
• Research-based teaching   The associate professor is also required to possess good interpersonal and communicative skills.

  Desired qualifications: 

   	
• Strong, independent research record in neurodegenerative disease, with expertise in mass spectrometry-based proteomics and biofluid biomarker discovery. 	
• Experience integrating multi-omics data with machine learning and AI, and working with preclinical models and cell-type-resolved approaches. 	
• A track record of securing competitive external funding and of research leadership. 	
• Teaching experience and formal teaching qualifications (e.g. Universitetspædagogikum), together with supervision experience. 	
• Ability to bridge discovery and translation (from molecule to patient) and to collaborate across academia, clinic, and industry, including innovation and spin-out activity   Terms of employment
 The position is a time limited position for 5 years. The average weekly working hours are 37 hours per week.

  Salary and other terms and conditions of appointment are set in accordance with the Agreement between the Ministry of Finance and AC (Danish Confederation of Professional Associations) or other relevant professional organisations.

  You can read more about salary levels in the state sector www.loenoverblik.dk (in Danish). 

  The position is covered by the Job Structure for Academic Staff at Universities 2025.
 
 Questions
 For further information, please contact Head of Department Dan Stærk, ds@sund.ku.dk. For information about the Department of Drug Design and Pharmacology and the Faculty of Health and Medical Sciences (SUND), please see www.drug.ku.dk and https://sund.ku.dk/.

  
 Foreign applicants may find this link useful: https://www.ism.ku.dk/ (International Staff Mobility).
 
 Application
 The application must be submitted in English and must include the following documents:

   	
• Application, including motivations for applying for the position (maximum 1 page) 	
• Curriculum vitae, including information about external funding 	
• Diplomas (Master’s, PhD, and other relevant certificates) 	
• A complete list of publications 	
• Research plan (3-5 pages) 	
• Uploads of maximum 5 (associate professors) publications to be considered in the assessment 	
• Teaching plan 	
• Teaching portfolio (Guidelines: https://employment.ku.dk/faculty/recruitment-process/job-application-portfolio)   Application procedure
 After the expiry of the deadline for applications, the authorized recruitment manager selects applicants for assessment on the advice of the Appointments Committee.  All applicants are then immediately notified whether their application has been passed for assessment. The Dean then appoints an expert assessment committee in order to make an assessment of the selected applicants for the specific post. Selected applicants are notified of the composition of the committee, and each applicant has the opportunity to comment on the part of the assessment that relates to the applicant him/herself. You can read about the recruitment process at The university's Job Portal.

  Please note that the applicant will be contacted if the assessment committee requires further documentation.

  The applicant will be assessed according to the Ministerial Order no. 242 of 13 March 2012 on the Appointment of Academic Staff at Universities.

  The University of Copenhagen encourages all interested applicants to apply for this position.

  Please submit the application with the required attachments. The closing date for applications is 23.59 CET on 20 November 2026.
